title: Three-Bean Salad
subtitle: Cannellini, kidney and chickpeas in a sharp herb vinaigrette
excerpt: Three types of tinned beans tossed with red onion, celery and flat-leaf parsley in a sharp herb vinaigrette. A classic American diner salad that takes five minutes to assemble and keeps for three days.
sourceNotes: Three-bean salad is a classic of American diner and church supper cooking, dating from at least the 1950s. The original version typically combined green beans, kidney beans and wax beans in a sweet vinegar dressing. The modern British and American version, using three types of tinned legume, appeared as tinned pulses became standard store cupboard ingredients. The formula is documented in countless American community and church cookbooks from the postwar period.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps for 3 days. Flavour improves overnight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made at least 30 minutes ahead. Can be made a day before.

content.text: Three-bean salad is a pantry salad that takes five minutes to make and gets better the longer it sits. The vinaigrette softens the beans slightly and penetrates the skins; a salad made the night before is noticeably better than one made an hour before. Use well-drained, well-rinsed tinned beans; any residual tin liquid makes the dressing murky.

Drain all three tins of beans thoroughly and rinse under cold water. Pat dry with kitchen paper. Combine the beans, red onion, celery and most of the parsley in a large bowl. Whisk together {{white-wine-vinegar}} of white wine vinegar, {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{caster-sugar}} of sugar, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Pour over the beans and toss to coat. Leave for at least 30 minutes before serving. Scatter the remaining parsley over the top.

items.cause: Beans not rinsed and dried thoroughly.
items.fix: Rinse well in a colander, shake out the excess water, then spread on kitchen paper and pat dry before adding to the bowl.

items.cause: Vinegar is heavy relative to the oil.
items.fix: The sugar in the dressing is meant to balance the sharpness; make sure it dissolves. Add another half teaspoon of sugar or a little more oil.

content.text: Three-bean salad has been a staple of American community cooking since the 1950s, appearing in countless potluck and picnic contexts. It crossed into British cooking as tinned pulses became a store cupboard standard. It is not glamorous, but it feeds many people from inexpensive ingredients, keeps for days, and needs no cooking at all.
